vulnerability.title: Ensure auditd Collects System Administrator Actions - /etc/sudoers.d/
vulnerability.description: At a minimum, the audit system should collect administrator actions for all users and root. If the auditd daemon is configured to use the augenrules program to read audit rules during daemon startup (the default), add the following lines to a file with suffix .rules in the directory /etc/audit/rules.d: -w /etc/sudoers.d/ -p wa -k actions If the auditd daemon is configured to use the auditctl utility to read audit rules during daemon startup, add the following lines to /etc/audit/audit.rules: -w /etc/sudoers.d/ -p wa -k actions
vulnerability.recommendation: Remediation script: # Remediation is applicable only in certain platforms if rpm --quiet -q audit && rpm --quiet -q kernel-core; then # Perform the remediation for both possible tools: 'auditctl' and 'augenrules' # Create a list of audit *.rules files that should be inspected for presence and correctness # of a particular audit rule. The scheme is as follows: # # ----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- # Tool used to load audit rules | Rule already defined | Audit rules file to inspect | # ----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- # auditctl | Doesn't matter | /etc/audit/audit.rules | # ----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- # augenrules | Yes | /etc/audit/rules.

triage_decision.reason: Adding an audit rule to monitor changes to /etc/sudoers.d/ is a standard STIG hardening action that does not alter system functionality or security posture beyond enabling logging. It follows the policy for safe remediation of audit rules.

reasoning_messages.reasoning:
We must produce plan, call review_plan. So need to draft plan. Considering rule: add audit rule to monitor /etc/sudoers.d/. Determine if audit rules loaded via augenrules. We will check if /etc/audit/audit.rules exists; if it holds, we can check.

But the goal: add rule in /etc/audit/rules.d/ - not file. So plan: create file /etc/audit/rules.d/sudoers.rules with required rule if augenrules is used. Need to check if auditd uses augenrules. In Rocky Linux, default uses augenrules. So we need to create file /etc/audit/rules.d/sudoers.rules with content "-w /etc/sudoers.d/ -p wa -k actions". Ensure file exists and correct content. Use read_file to inspect if file exists and if rule exists already. If file exists and contains the rule, nothing to do. If missing, create file. Also check for duplicate lines.

Potentially might use sed to modify? But easier: write_file to create. So plan: Check if /etc/audit/rules.d/sudoers.rules exists via read_file. If not, create. If exists, we need to ensure it contains the required line. We'll use grep? But we cannot chain commands; but we can use run_cmd individually. We'll use cat or grep? The rule: read_file then modify content string.

So steps: read_file /etc/audit/rules.d/sudoers.rules. If output contains " -w /etc/sudoers.d/ -p wa -k actions" then ok. If not, update file: either append or modify. But requirement: Do not duplicate. We'll just append if not present. So we will generate new content: current content + "\n-w /etc/sudoers.d/ -p wa -k actions\n". Then write_file.

Edge: file might not exist. read_file may produce error? The function will read file; if not exist might error. We'll need to handle that. But our plan description: if file missing, create file with content. So note. Also ensure permissions; default mode 0644.

Thus plan description can be described.

We need to call review_plan with plan_description. We'll produce a single plan string. Then wait for evaluation.

review_feedback: The plan addresses augenrules but does not cover the auditctl scenario. It also omits reloading auditd to apply changes. Therefore the plan would not fully resolve the vulnerability on all platforms.

previous_review_verdicts.feedback: The plan addresses augenrules but does not cover the auditctl scenario. It also omits reloading auditd to apply changes. Therefore the plan would not fully resolve the vulnerability on all platforms.
concerns: Does not handle auditctl configuration when auditd is started via auditctl.
No action to reload/restart auditd after adding the rule.
Potential duplicate rule entries were not fully validated.
Reliance on augenrules assumes system uses that loader, which may not be true on all systems.
suggested_improvements: Detect whether auditctl or augenrules is used and apply rule to the appropriate file (/etc/audit/audit.rules or /etc/audit/rules.d/*.rules).
After modifying the rule file, run 'augenrules --load' or 'service auditd restart' (or 'auditctl -R' for auditctl) to apply changes immediately.
Ensure the rule file is owned by root and has 0644 permissions before writing.
Check for and collapse duplicate rule entries before appending new ones.
